- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model consistently under-estimates true price after a spike (e.g., 80+ → 85+), especially if sentiment was neutral or slightly positive; add 2–5% buffer to forecast after spikes.  
- Model shows mean reversion bias: over-forecasting after sharp declines, under-forecasting after sharp rises — adjust by adding 1–3% to forecast if recent price moved >5% in 3 days.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is often too conservative; if sentiment is trending upward, add 1–2% to forecast for 30d horizon to capture momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.2 → +0.4), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment turning points, not just historical mean.
